map.拉伸强度 = 最大力 / (宽度 × 厚度)；扯断伸长率 = (断裂标距 - 原: Tensile strength = maximum force / (width × thickness); elongation at break = (gauge length at break - original gauge length) / original gauge length × 100%. Unit: MPa = N/mm².
map.📚 深度解析：橡胶拉伸强度计算: 📚 In-depth analysis: Rubber Tensile Strength Calculation
map.物性达标判定：按 GB/T 528 哑铃型试片测最大力，工具用宽度×厚度得截面积: Physical property compliance judgement: measure the maximum force on a GB/T 528 dumbbell specimen; the tool uses width × thickness for the cross-sectional area and computes the tensile strength in MPa and the elongation at break as a percentage, for acceptance against the product standard.
map.配方改进验证：对比补强前后拉伸强度与伸长率，判断炭黑/白炭黑用量是否合理，指导配: Formulation improvement verification: compare tensile strength and elongation before and after reinforcement to judge whether the carbon black or silica loading is reasonable, guiding formulation iteration.
map.等级评估：拉伸 ≥20MPa 且伸长 ≥300% 判「高强度高伸长」，适合动态受: Grade assessment: tensile ≥ 20 MPa and elongation ≥ 300% is rated high strength and high elongation, suitable for dynamically loaded parts such as tyre treads and drive belts; lower values mean the cure or reinforcement needs adjusting.
map.算例：最大力 500N、宽 6mm、厚 2mm、标距 25mm、断裂 125mm: Worked example: maximum force 500 N, width 6 mm, thickness 2 mm, gauge length 25 mm, break at 125 mm
map.为什么用截面积而不是横截面周长？: Why use the cross-sectional area rather than the cross-section perimeter?
map.拉伸强度定义为最大拉力除以试样最小截面积（宽×厚），单位为 MPa（N/mm²）: Tensile strength is defined as the maximum tensile force divided by the minimum cross-sectional area of the specimen, width × thickness, in MPa (N/mm²); using the perimeter underestimates the true stress, and GB/T 528 explicitly specifies the product of width and thickness in the central parallel section of the dumbbell as the effective cross-sectional area.
map.伸长率受标距影响吗？: Is elongation affected by the gauge length?
map.扯断伸长率 = (断裂距 − 初始标距)/初始标距 ×100%，与标距取值有关；: Elongation at break = (length at break − initial gauge length) / initial gauge length × 100%, so it depends on the gauge length used; standard specimens have a fixed gauge length, for example 25 mm for type I, and results from different gauge lengths cannot be compared directly, as they must be tested under the same standard.
